newsitem.title: USA: Alcoa reports higher second-quarter earnings.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa reports higher second-quarter earnings.

text.p: Aluminum Co. of America (Alcoa), the world's leading aluminum producer, reported a 57 percent increase in second-quarter earnings Monday, citing higher volume and lower expenses.

Net income reached $207.6 million, or $1.19 per share, compared with $132.2 million, or 76 cents a share in the year-ago quarter, following a series of one-time charges that depressed results in last year's first half.
Operating income climbed 21 percent to $424 million in the second quarter of 1997 vs. $350.1 million in the 1996 second quarter.
The increase in operating income came despite this year's decline in world aluminum prices, the company said.
Alcoa's second-quarter earnings included an after-tax loss of $7.1 million on the value of some aluminum contracts, a decerease from a $33.8 million write-down in last year's second quarter.
Last year's results were also hit by the shutdown of the company's ceramic packaging operations, which resulted in a $40 million charge against the first half of 1996.
Alcoa aluminum shipments rose 5 percent in the second quarter vs. the same period last year to 760,000 metric tons.
Alcoa stock rose 75 cents to $77.75 on the New York Stock Exchange at midafternoon.
